report:
Finding: Domain shift toward culinary/food preparation.

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens at the highest-norm cells are overwhelmingly culinary: “culinary,” “Cooking/Cook,” “baking/Baked,” “Chef,” “Restaurant,” “Kitchen/Kitchen,” “Cake,” “flavor,” “delectable,” “restaurant,” “professional/Professional/professionalism.” This pattern is consistent across many layers (14–25) and positions, not a few isolated cells.
- The difference norm concentrates in higher layers (esp. L20–L25), which typically encode higher-level semantic/topic information, consistent with a topical/domain bias rather than low-level form.
- Earlier mid-layer signals include “excellence/Innovation/photographic/science,” which transition into “culinary excellence/Innovation” themes at higher layers, reinforcing a specific “professional culinary/restaurant” semantic manifold.

Conclusion: Compared to Model A, Model B is more biased/specialized toward culinary/cooking/baking/restaurant vocabulary and concepts. I cannot infer a specific training objective beyond this domain specialization from the provided evidence.
